item.title: I got suspended from twitter again!! 2026-05-25
Coaching and outcomes
item.description: Last updated: 2026-05-22 See also My model of coaching, Coaching prerequisites Context My current aim with coaching/co-thinking (see e.g. cothinker-website.vercel.app/) is to: Create a portfolio of problems and solutions Make a living As I discussed at Meta-problem-solving, I imagine that there is a set of “meta-problems” that people have, problems they have about how they face their problems, and this is what coaching is particularly good for addressing As such, I want to get clients to explore this space, see how many meta-problems I can find, and also see how trying to solve each of them goes So each client below gets treated as an experiment: presenting symptoms, the underlying problems, hypotheses, and outcome reports at 1 week / 2 weeks / 1 month / 3 months Note that I’ve used Claude Code to compile the below, if it smells a bit LLM-y (A) Had 2-week sprint, now on retainer Ediya: Stuckness due to unclear brand philosophy Initial 2-week sprint 2026-04-20 → 2026-05-03; now on retainer Cadence: near-daily during sprint, lighter touch on retainer Source for outcome data: Ediya testimonial interview 2026-04-28 Presenting symptoms “This is killing me” — stuck for 3+ years on brand philosophy; couldn’t confidently make videos or try new formats [block] that was draining aliveness Online course ~80% drafted, stalled by perfectionism Fears around [block] Multiple possible offerings competing for attention with no clear sequence Underlying problems (my hypothesis) Lack of clear philosophy / mission was the load-bearing block Raw material was already internal — extraction and synthesis problem, not from-scratch discovery 3 years of unsuccessful self-attempts had snowballed into meta-stuckness: self-doubt about whether she could ever crack it Hypothesis If we extract and crystallise the philosophy first, everything downstream (course shape, freebie, journey video, sequencing) collapses into ordinary execution (and then I can also help with the execution via e.g.

item.title: "I can improve people's lives", 2026-05-21
item.description: This thought is an “A” for me, “A”s, that I just had for the first time (explicitly, at least) Obviously the implicit claim of e.g. getting a job is “I have skills and can help”, but I think it’s easy to approach it with more of a scarcity mindset + low self esteem The co-thinking offering spun out from helping people and being like “oh shit, I’m actually good at this, and people are benefitting?” So, it’s been an implicit claim for a while, but it feels good to make it explicit: I can improve people’s lives The whole claim of my co-thinking site/offering is that it’s not rocket science.
